data.long_meaning: The name Gangaadatt is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Ganga' meaning 'river' and 'datt' meaning 'given'. This name is a reference to the Hindu mythology where the Goddess Ganga is believed to have given life to the king Sahasrarjuna by descending from the heavens as a river. The name Gangaadatt carries the meaning “Ganga's gift” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Gangaadatt usually hope their child will grow to embody ganga's gift and live with faith, good character and purpose.

It is a name that is traditionally passed down through generations as a reminder of the rich heritage and mythology of Hinduism.

This name can serve as a reminder of the selfless and compassionate acts of the divine and inspire individuals to be more giving and compassionate in their own lives.
